To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a mixture of normal distributions can be used to describe plasma beta-mannsoidase activity in Salers cattle, that the distributions are not necessarily normal, that the distributions have different parameters and that the distributions are best described by a diallelic genetic model of inheritance.

a maximum likelihood approach for estimating genotype frequencies from laboratory assay data of plasma enzyme activity is feasible for the Salers breed, that estimates of gene frequency are high and that the test is more effective when animals are assayed as calves.
the plasma enzyme assay for beta-mannsosidosis in cattle can be used to estimate carrier probabilities and that the assay is more accurate for females than males and for calves than adults.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of genotype distributions from a mixture of distributions and provides an alternative to the traditional maximum likelihood approach for estimation of gene and carrier frequencies.
developing a method of estimating the parameters of a mixture of distributions and using the estimates to make inferences about the underlying genotype distributions and genotype fitness.

the development of statistical models for the estimation of genotype distributions and the estimation of genotype frequencies and probabilities of genotype assignment from data on a mixture of genotype distributions, and the estimation of systematic variation in the phenotype of each genotype distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the plasma assay for beta-mannsoidosis in Salers is effective in identifying carriers, but that the effectiveness is less for males than for females, and that the effectiveness is enhanced by averaging repeated measurements of enzyme activity.
a single plasma beta-mannoidase assay is an effective diagnostic test for beta-mannoidosis in Salers calves.
beta-mannosidoses in Salers cattle are inherited as a diallelic autosomal trait with gene frequency of 7.4%.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the maximum likelihood method can be used to simultaneously estimate all parameters of interest, and it can be applied to a variety of diagnostic tests.

the plasma assay for beta-mannnosidosis in cattle is effective for identifying carriers, but the effectiveness of this test depends on the animal age, sex, season of testing, and number of repeated measurements.
it is important to consider the genotype distribution of a predictive variable and the distribution of the variable itself when assessing the value of a diagnostic test.
